I'm requesting changes. The PR might be right, but I can't check it against the docstring, which the teammate said is the source of truth. The diff doesn't include the docstring or the tests, and the PR has no description saying which rules it implements or showing that the tests pass.

The change adds three rules: keep words with mixed case as-is, capitalize small words when they come first, last, or after a colon, and capitalize everything else. These are common title-case rules, and I don't see logic written just to pass a particular test. I'm not flagging any.

Problems I can see in the diff alone:

1. **The mixed-case check changes more than intended.** `any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:])` keeps any word with a capital after its first letter, including all-caps words. So "HELLO WORLD" stays "HELLO WORLD" instead of becoming "Hello World". If the docstring only means to keep things like "iPhone" or "McDonald", this is a regression. It also runs before the small-word check, so an all-caps "THE" in the middle of a title stays "THE" instead of becoming "the". Please confirm the docstring allows both.

2. **The colon check is fragile.** `result[-1].endswith(":")` looks at the previous word after it has been changed. That works here because no rule removes a colon, but checking the original `words[index-1]` would be clearer and wouldn't depend on how the rules are ordered.

3. **Edge cases don't match the other checks.** The "last word" check ignores empty strings from repeated spaces (`split(" ")` creates them). Also, `word.capitalize()` lowercases the rest of the word, and that's now the only path for words the mixed-case rule doesn't keep. Fine if the docstring says so; please confirm.

4. **No description.** Please add one that quotes the docstring rules you implemented, lists which failing tests are now fixed, and confirms the full suite passes with the tests unchanged.

To merge, I need the docstring quoted and the test run shown, plus the all-caps behavior fixed or explicitly justified by the docstring.
